themes_detail.label: Street Condition Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints spiked to 32 THIS WEEK, a 524% increase from the 5.1-per-week baseline over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 6.97), suggesting a sudden infrastructure failure or pothole epidemic affecting Central Harlem.
evidence: 32 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 5.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 6.97)
524% spike indicates acute, not chronic, deterioration
Aligns with CB budget requests for street/maintenance upgrades that recur annually, suggesting systemic neglect now accelerating
reporting_angles: Map specific blocks or corridors with highest complaint density; investigate if recent thaw/freeze cycle or deferred maintenance is culprit
Interview DOT on response timeline; cross-check with DOB permit data to see if ongoing street work is exacerbating conditions

themes_detail.label: Vendor Enforcement Surge
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints jumped to 3 THIS WEEK from a near-zero baseline of 0.1 per week (z-score: 8.69, 2300% spike), indicating either a sudden crackdown by city agencies or new street vending activity disrupting residents in Central Harlem.
evidence: 3 vendor enforcement complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (z-score: 8.69, 2300% increase)
Spike is entirely new phenomenon in recent 8-week data
Could signal new city enforcement blitz or influx of informal vending
reporting_angles: Contact DSNY/Parks Enforcement to confirm if they launched new vendor compliance sweep this week
Interview street vendors and residents: are unlicensed vendors proliferating, or is enforcement disproportionate?

themes_detail.label: Graffiti Outbreak
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints surged to 7 THIS WEEK, a 1020% increase from the 0.6-per-week baseline (z-score: 7.44), suggesting a sudden spike in vandalism or deteriorating neighborhood conditions in Central Harlem.
evidence: 7 graffiti complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average (z-score: 7.44, 1020% spike)
Unprecedented volume in recent baseline period
May correlate with street condition spike—suggests broader public space neglect or gang activity
reporting_angles: Map graffiti locations to identify if concentrated in one precinct or dispersed; check for tags/crews
Interview NYPD and Parks on removal timelines; cross-reference with street condition complaints for overlap in neighborhoods

themes_detail.label: Drinking Water Quality Concern
themes_detail.summary: Drinking water complaints hit 3 approximately 3 WEEKS AGO, a 1100% spike from the 0.2-per-week baseline (z-score: 6.35), followed by water conservation complaints spiking to 6 LAST WEEK (433% increase from 1.1 avg), suggesting potential water system stress or quality issues affecting Central Harlem.
evidence: Drinking water complaints: 3 (3 weeks ago) vs. 0.2 weekly average (z-score: 6.35, 1100% spike)
Water conservation complaints: 6 (last week) vs. 1.1 weekly average (z-score: 4.63, 433% spike)
Cluster of related water issues (quality, conservation, leaks all elevated) suggests systemic DEP problem
reporting_angles: Request DEP water quality data for Central Harlem; check for boil water advisories, main breaks, or contamination incidents in past 3 weeks
Interview residents on water discoloration, taste, smell; cross-check with plumbing complaints (980 total over 90 days) to see if burst mains are cause

themes_detail.label: Asbestos Concern (Older Data)
themes_detail.summary: Asbestos complaints registered 3 approximately 3 WEEKS AGO, a 1100% spike from the 0.2-per-week baseline (z-score: 6.35), suggesting either renovation work exposing asbestos or residents discovering hazardous materials in Central Harlem buildings.
evidence: Asbestos complaints: 3 (3 weeks ago) vs. 0.2 weekly average (z-score: 6.35, 1100% spike)
DOB data shows 440 alteration filings in past 90 days (370 alterations)—likely source of asbestos disturbance
Converges with maintenance/facility complaints also spiking 3 weeks ago (300% increase, 30 complaints)
reporting_angles: Cross-reference asbestos complaints with DOB alteration permits to identify buildings undergoing unsafe renovation
Investigate if property owners are following asbestos abatement protocols; interview NYC Department of Health on enforcement actions
